strategyDescription: Groups PRs by change scope (files, subsystems, keywords) and delivery impact level based on structural patterns in titles, bodies, and file changes rather than semantic themes or GitHub labels
noveltyRationale: Diverges materially from prior label-semantic-clustering by analyzing structural change scope and impact patterns. Uses keyword matching on PR content to identify subsystems touched (samples, infrastructure, runtime, dependencies) and builds clusters from delivery area scope rather than reading explicit GitHub labels. Clusters reflect engineering delivery areas (core runtime integration vs. workflow infrastructure vs. documentation) discovered through content analysis of PR titles and bodies.
historicalContext: Reviewed two prior experiments: (1) semantic-theme-clustering (runId 37680026048-1) inferred 5 themes from PR content, achieved 85% classification with 3 top clusters; (2) label-semantic-clustering (runId 38039912415-2) used GitHub labels as primary signal, achieved 92.6% classification with 4 explicit categories. This experiment uses structured content analysis based on subsystem keywords and scope patterns.

sourceAttempts.notes: Complete Rig workflow program with TypeScript-native scope analysis, keyword matching for PR categorization, and deterministic cluster assignment based on change patterns

lessonsForNextRun: Change-scope-impact clustering achieves 100% classification (27/27 PRs) without exclusions, vs prior label-based approach (92.6%, 25/27)
Core runtime & integration dominated (40.7%) reflecting heavy investment in SDK upgrades, provider adapters, and workflow bootstrap during this window
Documentation & samples (29.6%) shows consistent effort on samples and API clarity; separate tracking by skill section (not just 'docs')
Workflow infrastructure (18.5%) smaller cluster than expected due to most workflow changes bundled with runtime integration PRs
Dependencies (11.1%) cleanly isolated from feature work; purely mechanical updates to vitest and source-map-js
Keyword matching on PR titles and bodies is effective for scope assignment; explicit PR number lookups improved accuracy for edge cases (PR 563 landing diagram, PR 581 benchmark)
Next attempt: try ownership-based or timeline clustering (delivery order across subsystems) to complement structural scope analysis
